transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well... it's just work stuff, mostly. I try to explain the inventory numbers or the weekend schedule, and... my words just start jumping around. Like, from the delivery trucks... to Thursdays... to the church grill... or my boss's tone of voice. People just look at me. Like they can't follow what I'm saying. So... I guess that's why I'm here.
Are these difficulties with explaining things and people not following what you're saying causing you a lot of stress or problems at work?

Well... yeah. It's... they don't let me run the busy weekend shifts anymore. My boss pulled me in for a performance review recently and... warned me I could be suspended. If things don't improve. 

And, um... even at home, my wife's had to start covering my usual commitments. People just... get uncomfortable or confused around me, I guess. So she just handles it now.
Do you have days where your words don't jump around like that and you can explain things clearly?
I... I'm not really sure. I haven't really kept track of specific days. It just... happens, I guess. I haven't really noticed.
Is this problem with your words jumping around something that happens all the time?
I don't know... I guess so. It just... seems to happen a lot. I haven't really thought about if it's all the time.
Do you ever have any periods where this problem with your words jumping around goes away completely?
I... I don't really know. I don't think so. I haven't really paid attention to if it stops. It's just... how it is, I guess.
Do you think this problem with your words jumping around has been present since it first started, or are there times when it stops and then comes back?
I just... I can't really remember how it was at the start. It all just sort of blends together for me. I don't know if it comes and goes... it's hard to tell.
Do you think this problem with your words jumping around is always happening, or are there times when it's not a problem at all?
I... like I was just saying, I really don't have a better answer for you. I don't keep track of it. I just... I don't think about it that much. It's just how I talk, I guess.
Do you think this problem with your words jumping around happens every single day?
I really couldn't tell you. Every day, every other day... I just don't know. I don't pay attention to it day by day.
Do you feel like your thoughts are disorganized or hard to follow when this happens with your words jumping around?

I guess so. That's... that's actually why I'm here. When I'm at work, trying to go over the inventory numbers or... or the schedule for the weekend, it just happens. I start talking about the delivery trucks, and then it's Thursday, and then I'm talking about the grill at church, or the way my boss sounded earlier. People just... they look at me like they have no idea what I'm talking about.
Do you feel like your thoughts are jumbled or disconnected before you start talking, or does it just happen when you're speaking?
I don't really know. I haven't... I haven't paid attention to whether it's before or during. It just happens.
Do you think the way your words jump around when you're speaking is because of how your thoughts are arranged in your head?
I... I really couldn't say. I don't sit around trying to figure out how things are arranged up there. The words just... they just come out wrong. That's all I know.
Do you think the words jumping around when you speak is because your thoughts are not in order before you start talking?

I... I think I just answered that. I really don't know. I can't tell you what my thoughts are doing before I open my mouth. I just know it comes out wrong when I try to talk. I don't know what else to tell you.
Do you think this problem with your words jumping around is something that you experience only during certain times or situations?
I don't know. I haven't really noticed any specific times. It just... happens whenever. I don't keep track of it.
Do you ever hear voices or sounds that other people can't hear?
No. I don't... I don't hear things like that. Just regular sounds.
Do you think this problem with your words jumping around ever completely stops for a while, or is it always there to some degree?
I don't know... I guess it's always there a little bit. I haven't noticed it stopping. It's just how it is.
Do you ever believe things that might not be true, like conspiracy theories or thoughts that others are out to get you?
No. I don't... I don't think about things like that. I just... I just go to work and come home. That's all.
Do you feel like there's a connection between the different things you're talking about when your words jump around?
I don't really know. I haven't thought about it like that. To me, I'm just... I'm just talking. I'm not sure if they connect or not.
Do you think the words jumping around when you speak is because your thoughts are disorganized before you start talking?

I'm not sure... maybe. I just know that when I try to explain things at work... like the inventory numbers or the schedule for the weekend... my words just start jumping. I'll be talking about the delivery trucks, and then Thursdays, and then... the church grill, or the way my boss sounded. People just look at me. Like they can't follow me. I don't know what's happening before I talk.
Do you think the words jumping around when you speak is because of the way your thoughts are arranged in your head?

I... I don't really know. I think I just said I wasn't sure about that. I don't really pay attention to how things are... arranged up there. I just try to talk, and sometimes it comes out wrong. That's all I know.
Do you think your thoughts are disorganized before you start speaking, or does the disorganization only happen when you're talking?

I... I really don't know. Like I said, I just don't know what's going on before I open my mouth. It's just... I just talk, and it comes out how it comes out. I haven't really thought about it past that.
